Nvidia, il board esclude il ritorno di Jensen Huang. Trump lo sostiene, il titolo crolla

20261116-21014394f1.caption:
Il board di Nvidia non valuta il ritorno di Jensen Huang come amministratore delegato.

Secondo una fonte sentita da CNBC, il consiglio si concentra sull'indagine affidata allo studio Wachtell Lipton. Huang si è dimesso giovedì scorso, dopo 33 anni alla guida, per le notizie su alcune relazioni extraconiugali. Una sarebbe con una presunta spia cinese. Donald Trump si dice favorevole a un suo ritorno, e una petizione firmata anche da Elon Musk ha superato le 165.000 firme. Secondo il Guardian, lunedì il titolo ha aperto in calo del 2,7%.

Secondo voi, il futuro di Nvidia dipende ancora da Huang?

Fonti: Financial Times, CNBC, The Guardian, ANSA, Al Jazeera.

c.titolo_copertina: Nvidia, il board non valuta il ritorno di Jensen Huang. Trump: «Potrebbe tornare»

slide.testo: Il cofondatore si è dimesso giovedì scorso. Giorni prima aveva ammesso una relazione extraconiugale. Secondo la stampa, una sarebbe con Alice Huang, dirigente del cliente Megaspeed di Singapore, presunta spia cinese. Megaspeed afferma che lei ha lasciato la società a fine 2025.

Secondo una fonte sentita da CNBC, il board non valuta il suo ritorno. Lo studio legale Wachtell Lipton indaga se la condotta di Huang abbia compromesso la sicurezza nazionale o segreti aziendali. Ad interim c'è la direttrice finanziaria Colette Kress.

slide.titolo: La Silicon Valley chiede di riaverlo
slide.testo: Il dato è del Guardian. Secondo Al Jazeera le firme sono 177.000, secondo CNBC 180.000. Tra chi ha firmato ci sono Elon Musk, Garry Tan di Y Combinator e Tim Sweeney di Epic Games.

slide.titolo: La Casa Bianca apre al ritorno
slide.testo: Potrebbe tornare. C'è un grande gruppo di persone che vorrebbe che tornasse.
slide.autore: Donald Trump, presidente degli Stati Uniti

slide.titolo: Capitalizzazione in calo dopo lo scandalo
slide.testo: Secondo il Guardian, Nvidia valeva 4.500 miliardi di dollari prima dello scandalo. Lunedì il titolo ha aperto a -2,7%, secondo ANSA è poi sceso a -4,68%. Gli analisti stimano che senza Huang potrebbe perdere fino al 25-30% del valore.

slide.titolo: Washington stringe sui chip diretti in Cina
slide.testo: Il Dipartimento del Commercio USA impone licenze di esportazione per i chip più avanzati a Singapore, Thailandia, Malesia, Indonesia e Brasile. L'obiettivo è impedire di aggirare i limiti usando data center in paesi terzi. Intanto il board cerca un nuovo amministratore delegato.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: Nvidia produce i chip alla base dell'intelligenza artificiale. Le sue oscillazioni pesano su Wall Street e sui risparmi investiti nei titoli tecnologici. La stretta USA sull'export di chip cambia le regole di un mercato da cui dipende tutta l'industria dell'IA.

sources.title: Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
sources.text:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity in order to discuss internal matters. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.
Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence, as well as affairs with employees at Nvidia.
Over the weekend, the Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.
A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.
Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.
An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.
President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia.
"It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before," Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns.
On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

sources.title: Trump backs calls for reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
sources.text:
Donald Trump has expressed support for the return of Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia, joining Silicon Valley heavyweights in backing the reinstatement of the AI figurehead.
The US president referred to a tech industry campaign for Huang’s rehabilitation, saying a “big group” of people would like him back.
“I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump told reporters as he left the White House on a trip to Asia. “He could return. There’s a big group of people that would like him to return.”
The comments came as the US government announced a crackdown on companies such as Nvidia selling AI chips and servers to overseas datacentres that in turn are supplying computing power to China and other US adversaries.
Elon Musk, the chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, and a host of other tech bosses have signed an open letter calling for the reinstatement of Huang. The former Nvidia CEO resigned last Thursday amid reports of extramarital liaisons, including with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who is no relation. Days before, Huang had admitted being unfaithful to his wife without specifying who was involved.
Trump said on Monday: “Nobody’s proven that she’s a spy. She may not be a spy.” Trump has faced questions after it was reported that a US intelligence report about Huang’s relationship with the alleged spy was circulated among senior figures in his administration.
The reinstatement letter has more than 165,000 signatories and demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.
Huang’s resignation ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded.
According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed with people close to him a possible return to the company. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return and would try to garner support from the White House. The FT also reported on Monday that Nvidia’s board was not considering reinstating Huang.
One analyst downplayed the prospect of a Huang return, describing the notion of the ex-CEO’s reinstatement as “ridiculous”. Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, said the range of issues facing Huang and Nvidia, from personal conduct to questions over China, made an external candidate or the permanent appointment of the interim CEO – Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer – the best option.
“We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO, and for the company the best path forward is with a new external CEO or Colette,” he said, describing the petition as “noise and distraction”.
The new rule announced by the US government on Monday requires companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted.
“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving datacentres in third countries,” the US Department of Commerce said.
Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy, worked as an executive at the Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. According to reports, Megaspeed is under suspicion of diverting powerful Nvidia chips to China in contravention of US export laws.
Megaspeed said on Sunday it was a “legitimate and lawful business” and that Huang had left the business in late 2025. It added that it complied “with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes, including United States export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate”.
Nvidia shares opened down 2.7% on Monday, knocking about $100bn (£75.8bn) off Nvidia’s market capitalisation, lowering it to $3.82tn compared with $4.5tn before the scandal broke.

sources.title: Musk, Silicon Valley insiders urge Nvidia to restore Jensen Huang as CEO
sources.text:
Musk, Silicon Valley insiders urge Nvidia to restore Jensen Huang as CEO
Nvidia faces potential 30 percent value loss without Jensen Huang, say market analysts amid stock downturn.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley insiders are calling on chipmaker Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned last week from the company he cofounded.
Musk is one of the 177,000 signatories to a petition titled “Stand With Jensen”, calling for the reinstatement of the executive, who resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
“We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA’s best interests,” the letter published on the petition’s website said.
More privately, a group of Silicon Valley insiders is pushing to get Huang back in the role, with the Financial Times reporting that Huang is considering a comeback. The paper reported that an unnamed group of Silicon Valley insiders has put together a so-called war room and is lobbying the White House for support which is a move that may have been successful.
“A lot of people are asking Jensen, they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” United States President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday.
Much of Nvidia’s value is tied to Huang, with analysts estimating that the company could lose as much as 25 to 30 percent of its value without him.
Nvidia’s stock was trending downward in early trading on Wall Street, with US markets opening down 2.3 percent on the day. Over the last five days, the stock has dropped 8.5 percent and is down more than 25.7 percent over the last month.
AI constraints
The developments come as the White House moves to designate Nvidia, along with more than two dozen other companies, as “national champions” in the artificial intelligence industry, a new initiative intended to help the company secure more business overseas, according to reporting by The Wall Street Journal.
They also come as the Trump administration issued a rule on Monday that it would restrict China’s access to chips made by companies including Nvidia, as Trump begins a trip to China where he will meet with President Xi Jinping.
The restrictions are aimed at preventing Chinese companies from “circumventing” existing limits by using data centres in Southeast Asian countries such as Malaysia and Thailand to train their AI models.
“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries,” the Department of Commerce said in a statement.
The new rule comes as the Commerce Department is scrambling to demonstrate that it is cracking down on Chinese access to sensitive US technology, following reports that the agency under Secretary Howard Lutnick turned a blind eye to the smuggling of advanced Nvidia AI chips into China.
